questions.stem: Which sentence has a mistake in grammar or usage? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: The dog chased it's tail around the yard.
She went to their house after school.
The cat licked its paws after eating.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: The word "it's" is short for "it is" or "it has," never a possessive, so "The dog chased it's tail" needs the possessive "its." The other two sentences use "their" and "its" correctly.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a mistake in grammar or usage? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: Me and her went to the store after class.
He and I finished the project together.
She and I are meeting them later today.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: A subject needs subject pronouns, so "Me and her went to the store" should be "She and I went." Test it alone: you would say "I went," not "Me went."

questions.stem: Which sentence has a mistake in grammar or usage? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: The car drove beside the river slowly.
She went out the door and into the garden.
He is waiting in the bus stop.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: You wait at a bus stop, not "in the bus stop," since you are not inside it. The prepositions in "beside the river" and "out the door and into the garden" are both fine.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a mistake in grammar or usage? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: Yesterday, I will finish my homework.
Tomorrow, I will go to the movies with my friends.
Last week, she attended the meeting.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: The word "Yesterday" points to the past, so "I will finish" clashes with it. The verb should be "I finished my homework." The other two sentences match their time words.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a mistake in grammar or usage? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: He completed his homework quick.
The children played happily in the yard.
She sings beautifully during the concert.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: Adverbs describe verbs, so "completed his homework quick" needs "quickly." The other two sentences already use the adverbs "happily" and "beautifully."

questions.stem: Which sentence has a mistake in grammar or usage? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: The childrens' toys were scattered everywhere.
The child's toy was missing from the shelf.
The women's coats were hanging by the door.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: The word "children" is already plural, so the possessive is "children's toys," not "childrens' toys." The forms "child's" and "women's" are both built correctly.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a mistake in grammar or usage? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: He is the more smarter student in the class.
She is the better of the two singers.
This is the best decision we could make.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: Never put "more" in front of an -er word. "The more smarter student in the class" should be "the smartest student," since a class holds more than two people.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a mistake in grammar or usage? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: Either I will attend the party, and I will stay home.
Both the boys and the girls are invited to the event.
She went to the store and bought some groceries.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: The word "Either" pairs with "or," not "and," so the sentence should read "Either I will attend the party, or I will stay home." The pairing "Both ... and" is correct.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a mistake in grammar or usage? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: They has finished their project last night.
He will be studying for the test tomorrow.
We were at the park when it started to rain.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: The pronoun "They" is plural, so it takes "have," not "has." Because "last night" is a finished past time, the sentence should read "They finished their project last night."

questions.stem: Which sentence has a mistake in grammar or usage? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: The teacher gave us ours assignments after class.
The students completed their assignments on time.
The dog chased its ball across the yard.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: The word "ours" stands alone and never sits in front of a noun, so "ours assignments" should be "our assignments." The words "their" and "its" are used correctly.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a mistake in grammar or usage? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: This is the most easiest question on the test.
He is taller than his friends.
She is better at math than her brother is.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: Never stack "most" on top of an -est word. "The most easiest question" should be simply "the easiest question." The comparatives "taller than" and "better than" are fine.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a mistake in grammar or usage? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: The cat slept under the bed during the storm.
She placed the book beside the laptop.
He waited in line for almost an hour.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: All three sentences are fine, so choose "No mistakes." The prepositions "under the bed," "beside the laptop" and "in line" all fit, and every verb matches its subject.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a mistake in grammar or usage? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: He drove very slow on the icy road.
The athlete performed wonderfully at the competition.
The cake tasted delicious after it was baked.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: A verb needs an adverb, so "drove very slow" should be "drove very slowly." The adverb "wonderfully" and the adjective "delicious" after the linking verb "tasted" are both correct.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a mistake in grammar or usage? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: Me and her will meet you at the restaurant.
He and I will attend the conference next week.
She and I went to the library together.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: A subject needs subject pronouns, so "Me and her will meet you" should be "She and I will meet you." You would say "I will meet you," not "Me will meet you."

questions.stem: Which sentence has a mistake in grammar or usage? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: She studied for the test last night and will finish it tomorrow.
He will finish his homework tonight.
I enjoyed the movie we watched yesterday.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: All three sentences are fine, so choose "No mistakes." The past tense "studied" matches "last night," "will finish" matches "tomorrow," and "enjoyed" matches "yesterday."

questions.stem: Which sentence has a mistake in grammar or usage? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: The teachers lounge is down the hall.
The student's books were left on the table.
The children's playground is closed today.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: A possessive noun needs an apostrophe, so "The teachers lounge" should be "The teachers' lounge." The forms "student's" and "children's" are punctuated correctly.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a mistake in grammar or usage? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: This is the most hardest test I've ever taken.
He felt worse after he heard the news.
She was happier when she got her new puppy.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: The word "hardest" is already a superlative, so "the most hardest test" should be just "the hardest test." The forms "worse" and "happier" are correct comparatives.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a mistake in grammar or usage? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: The wind blew through the trees all night.
The teacher had taught us the lesson by then.
He drove to the office early this morning.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: All three sentences are fine, so choose "No mistakes." "Blew" is the past tense of blow, "had taught" shows an action finished before "then," and "drove" matches "this morning."

questions.stem: Which sentence has a punctuation mistake? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: I need to buy apples, oranges, and bananas.
The teacher asked, "Did you finish your homework?"
We're planning to visit three cities: Paris London and Berlin.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: The list "Paris London and Berlin" is missing its commas. Items in a series need commas between them, so it should read "Paris, London and Berlin."

questions.stem: Which sentence has a punctuation mistake? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: The teacher asked, "Did you finish your homework"?
The dog ran outside without his leash!
I have three things to do today: clean, cook, and study.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: In "Did you finish your homework"? the question mark belongs inside the quotation marks, because the question is part of what the teacher actually said.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a punctuation mistake? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: We're planning to visit three cities: Paris, London, and Berlin.
I love running and biking, those are my favorite sports.
I enjoy hiking in the mountains; it's relaxing.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: "I love running and biking, those are my favorite sports" joins two complete sentences with only a comma. Use a semicolon or a period instead of that comma.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a punctuation mistake? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: I went to the store but I forgot my wallet.
We need to leave now, or we'll miss the train.
I want to go, but I can’t.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: "I went to the store but I forgot my wallet" needs a comma before "but." When "and," "but" or "or" joins two complete sentences, put a comma in front of it.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a punctuation mistake? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: He said, "I'll meet you at 5:00."
She exclaimed, "This is unbelievable!"
We stayed at the hotel for three days and it was lovely.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: "We stayed at the hotel for three days and it was lovely" is two complete sentences joined by "and," so a comma is needed before "and."

questions.stem: Which sentence has a punctuation mistake? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: We visited the park yesterday.
Do you think we should go now?
Is it raining outside?
No mistakes
questions.explanation: All three are punctuated correctly. The statement "We visited the park yesterday." ends with a period, and both of the questions end with question marks.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a punctuation mistake? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: Is it raining outside?
It's cold today, isn't it!
Do you know where my keys are?
No mistakes
questions.explanation: "It's cold today, isn't it!" is really a question, so it should end with a question mark. The tag "isn't it" is asking the reader to agree.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a punctuation mistake? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: My favorite activities are swimming, biking, and hiking.
We went to the park, and then to the zoo.
She asked, "Can you help me with this?"
No mistakes
questions.explanation: "We went to the park, and then to the zoo" has an extra comma. "And then to the zoo" is not a complete sentence, so no comma is needed before "and."

questions.stem: Which sentence has a punctuation mistake? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: I enjoy reading books they are a great way to relax.
I love baking cakes; they are fun to make.
I finished my homework, and now I’m going to relax.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: "I enjoy reading books they are a great way to relax" runs two complete sentences together with no punctuation. Add a period or a semicolon after "books."

questions.stem: Which sentence has a punctuation mistake? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: We need the following items: paper, pens, and tape.
The dinner was delicious; I had seconds.
We need to buy groceries, do laundry, and cook dinner.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: All three are correct. The colon introduces a list, the semicolon joins two complete sentences and the commas separate the items in a series.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a punctuation mistake? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: It's important to use punctuation correctly
She said, "I'm so excited for the trip."
The test was hard, but I passed it.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: "It's important to use punctuation correctly" never ends. Every sentence needs end punctuation, and this one is a statement, so it needs a period.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a punctuation mistake? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: She asked if I was going to the party?
He asked, "Where did you find that?"
The teacher asked, "Did you submit your assignment?"
No mistakes
questions.explanation: "She asked if I was going to the party?" only tells about a question, so it should end with a period. Use a question mark only when the sentence itself asks something.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a punctuation mistake? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: We traveled to Paris last year.
I stayed home all day.
We traveled to Rome, Italy.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: All three are correct. Two are plain statements ending in periods, and "We traveled to Rome, Italy." correctly puts a comma between the city and the country.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a punctuation mistake? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: The party was fun I stayed until midnight.
She loves reading books; they are her favorite pastime.
We had pizza, pasta, and salad for dinner.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: "The party was fun I stayed until midnight" jams two complete sentences together. Put a period or a semicolon after "fun" to separate them.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a punctuation mistake? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: She loves reading books about history.
She asked, "Are you coming to the meeting?"
She loves reading books they are her favorite.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: "She loves reading books they are her favorite" is a run-on. Two complete sentences need a period or a semicolon between them, not nothing at all.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a punctuation mistake? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: I think we should go; it's getting late.
We traveled to Spain; the beaches were beautiful.
The movie starts at 8:00, and we'll be late.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: All three are correct. Both semicolons join two complete sentences, and the comma before "and" in "The movie starts at 8:00, and we'll be late." is exactly right.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a punctuation mistake? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: My brother loves pizza, pasta, and salad.
I forgot my phone at home I had to go back.
I watched TV, did my homework, and went to bed.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: "I forgot my phone at home I had to go back" is two complete sentences with nothing between them. Add a period or a semicolon after "home."

questions.stem: Which sentence has a punctuation mistake? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: I read the book, it was amazing.
The pizza was delicious; I ate the whole thing.
I finished the report; it was well-written.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: "I read the book, it was amazing" uses a comma to join two complete sentences. That is called a comma splice; use a semicolon or a period instead.

questions.stem: Read the following sentences and choose the one that would make the best topic sentence for a paragraph about the benefits of regular exercise.
options: Regular exercise improves cardiovascular health, strengthens muscles, and enhances flexibility.
Many people do not get enough physical activity in their daily lives.
Eating a balanced diet is also important for maintaining good health.
Some exercises are more enjoyable than others.
questions.explanation: A topic sentence must be broad enough to cover every detail that follows, and the sentence naming better heart health, stronger muscles and more flexibility does that. 'Some exercises are more enjoyable than others' is only one narrow detail.

questions.stem: Which of the following sentences would best serve as the topic sentence for a paragraph about the importance of time management for students?
options: Some students prefer studying in the morning; while others study at night.
Effective time management allows students to balance academics and extracurricular activities.
Many schools offer workshops on how to manage time effectively.
Procrastination can lead to stress and poor academic performance.
questions.explanation: This question wants a topic sentence, which states the broad main idea. 'Effective time management allows students to balance academics and extracurricular activities' covers the whole paragraph, while the sentence about school workshops is just one supporting detail.

questions.stem: Select the sentence that would make the best topic sentence for a paragraph about the impact of technology on communication.
options: Smartphones have become an essential part of daily life.
Technology has revolutionized the way we communicate, making it faster and more convenient.
Many people use social media to stay connected with friends and family.
Some people prefer face-to-face communication over digital methods.
questions.explanation: A topic sentence states the main idea in a broad way. Saying technology has changed communication and made it faster covers everything, but 'Smartphones have become an essential part of daily life' narrows the paragraph to one device.

questions.stem: Choose the best topic sentence for a paragraph discussing the challenges of learning a new language.
options: Learning a new language can be difficult but rewarding.
Many schools offer foreign language classes.
Some languages are harder to learn than others.
Traveling abroad is a great way to practice language skills.
questions.explanation: You need a topic sentence broad enough to introduce the whole paragraph. 'Learning a new language can be difficult but rewarding' does that, while 'Some languages are harder to learn than others' is a single detail.

questions.stem: Identify the sentence that would best serve as the topic sentence for a paragraph about the effects of pollution on marine life.
options: Pollution affects not only the oceans but also the creatures that inhabit them.
Plastic waste is a major pollutant in the world's oceans.
Many marine animals mistake plastic for food.
Governments are implementing policies to reduce ocean pollution.
questions.explanation: A topic sentence announces the main idea instead of giving one example. The choice saying pollution affects the oceans and the creatures in them covers every detail, while the sentence about plastic waste is only one example.

questions.stem: Choose the word that best completes the sentence. She was praised for her ______ in completing the project ahead of schedule.
options: procrastination
diligence
indifference
negligence
questions.explanation: Look for the word that matches the clue in the sentence. Being praised for finishing early points to 'diligence,' which means steady, careful effort, while 'procrastination' and 'negligence' would earn blame instead.

questions.stem: Select the word that best completes the sentence. The teacher's explanation was so ______ that all the students understood the complex topic.
options: obscure
ambiguous
clear
confusing
questions.explanation: Use the clue in the rest of the sentence. Because all the students understood a complex topic, the explanation must have been 'clear,' while words like 'obscure' and 'confusing' mean the opposite.

questions.stem: Select the word that best completes the sentence. The scientist presented his findings at the conference to ______ his research.
options: hide
promote
disregard
hinder
questions.explanation: Ask why a scientist speaks at a conference. Presenting findings is a way to 'promote' research, meaning to help it get noticed, while 'hide' and 'hinder' work against the whole reason for presenting.

questions.stem: Choose the word that best completes the sentence. After months of preparation, the team was ______ to win the championship.
options: reluctant
eager
indifferent
hesitant
questions.explanation: Months of preparation build excitement, so the missing word must be positive. 'Eager' means very ready and excited, while 'reluctant,' 'hesitant' and 'indifferent' all suggest the team did not care.

questions.stem: Select the word that best completes the sentence. The artist's work was so ______ that it left the audience speechless.
options: mundane
uninspiring
breathtaking
ordinary
questions.explanation: Work that leaves an audience speechless must be amazing, so 'breathtaking' fits the clue. 'Mundane,' 'ordinary' and 'uninspiring' all mean dull, and dull work would not leave anyone speechless.

questions.stem: Topic: The benefits of recycling. Which sentence least supports the topic?
options: Recycling helps conserve natural resources by reusing materials.
Recycling reduces the amount of waste sent to landfills.
Some people enjoy watching movies on the weekends.
Recycling can save energy compared to producing new products from raw materials.
questions.explanation: This asks which sentence is off the paragraph's single subject. Saving resources, cutting landfill waste and saving energy all explain recycling, but weekend movies have nothing to do with it.

questions.stem: Topic: The importance of sleep for teenagers. Which sentence least supports the topic?
options: Adequate sleep helps improve concentration and academic performance.
Lack of sleep can lead to health issues like obesity and depression.
Many teenagers enjoy playing video games with friends.
Sleep is essential for growth and development during adolescence.
questions.explanation: The sentence that does not belong is the one off the paragraph's subject. Focus, health problems and growth all connect to teen sleep, while enjoying video games with friends is a different topic.

questions.stem: Topic: The effects of global warming. Which sentence least supports the topic?
options: Rising temperatures can lead to more extreme weather events.
Glaciers are melting; causing sea levels to rise.
Planting trees can help reduce carbon dioxide in the atmosphere.
Many people prefer to live in warmer climates.
questions.explanation: Look for the sentence that leaves the paragraph's subject. Extreme weather, melting glaciers and carbon dioxide all connect to global warming, but 'Many people prefer to live in warmer climates' is a personal preference, not an effect.

questions.stem: Topic: The advantages of learning to play a musical instrument. Which sentence least supports the topic?
options: Learning an instrument can improve cognitive skills and memory.
Playing music can be a form of stress relief and emotional expression.
Some instruments are more expensive than others.
Musicians often develop better coordination and discipline.
questions.explanation: The odd sentence is the one that does not support the topic. Better thinking, stress relief and coordination are all advantages of playing music, while the cost of instruments is about price, not benefits.

questions.stem: Topic: The impact of social media on society. Which sentence least supports the topic?
options: Social media platforms allow people to connect globally.
Excessive use of social media can lead to decreased face-to-face interactions.
Many people enjoy reading books in their free time.
Social media can influence public opinion and spread information rapidly.
questions.explanation: Pick the sentence that leaves the paragraph's subject. Connecting globally, less face-to-face time and shaping opinion are all effects of social media, but enjoying books in free time is unrelated.

questions.stem: Topic: The importance of healthy eating habits. Which sentence least supports the topic?
options: Eating a balanced diet provides the nutrients needed for energy and growth.
Healthy eating can prevent chronic diseases such as diabetes and heart disease.
Junk food is often high in calories but low in nutritional value.
Watching television is a common leisure activity.
questions.explanation: The sentence that least supports the topic is the one off subject. Nutrients, disease prevention and junk food all deal with eating, while watching television is a leisure habit, not a food choice.

questions.stem: Choose the sentence that best expresses the idea most clearly.
options: Due to the fact that it was raining; we had to cancel the picnic.
We had to cancel the picnic because it was raining.
The picnic was canceled on account of the fact that there was rain.
Owing to the rainy conditions; the picnic had to be canceled by us.
questions.explanation: The clearest sentence states the idea in the fewest plain words. 'We had to cancel the picnic because it was raining' is short and direct, while padding like 'due to the fact that' only adds words.

questions.stem: Choose the sentence that best expresses the idea most clearly.
options: The performance was enjoyed by the audience who applauded enthusiastically.
The audience applauded enthusiastically because they enjoyed the performance.
Because of their enjoyment, the audience was enthusiastic in their applause.
Enthusiastically applauding, the audience enjoyed the performance.
questions.explanation: Clear writing puts the doer first and states the cause plainly. 'The audience applauded enthusiastically because they enjoyed the performance' does both, while the other choices use passive wording or rearrange the idea awkwardly.

questions.stem: Choose the sentence that expresses the idea most clearly.
options: The book, which was written by the author, was interesting to read.
The author's book was interesting.
It was interesting to read the book that was authored by the writer.
The book was interesting.
questions.explanation: Choose the shortest wording that still keeps every piece of information. 'The author's book was interesting' drops the extra words but keeps the author, while 'The book was interesting' loses the author completely.

questions.stem: Select the sentence that best expresses the idea clearly.
options: The cake was baked by her in the kitchen yesterday.
She baked the cake in the kitchen yesterday.
In the kitchen yesterday, the cake was baked.
Yesterday, the kitchen was where the cake was baked by her.
questions.explanation: Active voice, with the doer first, is usually the clearest. 'She baked the cake in the kitchen yesterday' names who did the action, while the passive versions bury her behind 'was baked by.'

questions.stem: Choose the best word to join the sentences. 'I wanted to go for a walk. It was raining heavily.'
options: but
so
because
and
questions.explanation: This asks for the joining word that shows how the two ideas relate. Wanting a walk and heavy rain clash, so 'but' shows that contrast, while 'so' and 'because' would wrongly signal cause.

questions.stem: Select the word that best connects the sentences. 'She studied hard for the test. She earned a high score.'
options: However
Therefore
Although
Meanwhile
questions.explanation: Decide what the second sentence does to the first. Studying hard led to the high score, so 'Therefore' shows a result, while 'However' would signal a contrast that is not there.

questions.stem: Choose the best word to complete the sentence. 'He didn't see the stop sign, ______ he got a traffic ticket.'
options: unless
because
so
yet
questions.explanation: The connector must match the relationship between the two clauses. Missing the stop sign caused the ticket, so 'so' shows the result, while 'because' would reverse the cause and the effect.

questions.stem: Select the word that best joins the thoughts. 'The sun set. The stars began to appear.'
options: Because
While
As soon as
After
questions.explanation: Pick the word that shows the true time relationship. The stars appear once the sun has set, so 'After' fits, while 'As soon as' would claim they appeared instantly, which the sentences never say.

questions.stem: Choose the best word to join the sentences. 'He was tired, ______ he continued working.'
options: but
so
because
therefore
questions.explanation: Being tired and continuing to work do not match, so the joining word must show contrast. 'But' does that, while 'so' and 'therefore' would say being tired caused him to keep working.

questions.stem: Select the word that best connects the sentences. 'The team practiced every day. They won the championship.'
options: However
Because
Consequently
Meanwhile
questions.explanation: Daily practice led to the championship, so the connector should show a result. 'Consequently' means as a result, while 'However' signals contrast and 'Meanwhile' signals time.

questions.stem: Read the following paragraph and identify the sentence that does not belong.
options: The desert is a harsh environment with extreme temperatures and little water.
Many unique plants and animals have adapted to survive in these conditions.
Cacti store water in their thick stems to endure dry periods.
Tropical rainforests receive abundant rainfall throughout the year.
questions.explanation: The sentence that does not belong is the one off the paragraph's single subject. Every other sentence describes the desert, so 'Tropical rainforests receive abundant rainfall throughout the year' shifts to a completely different place.

questions.stem: Read the paragraph and choose the sentence that does not belong.
options: Baking bread requires patience and precision.
Measuring ingredients accurately is crucial for the desired outcome.
Some people prefer to cook savory dishes instead of baking.
Allowing the dough to rise properly affects the texture of the bread.
questions.explanation: Look for the sentence that leaves the subject. The paragraph explains how bread is baked, so measuring and rising fit, while a note about people who prefer savory cooking changes the subject.

questions.stem: Identify the sentence that does not fit in the following paragraph.
options: The invention of the printing press revolutionized the spread of information.
Before its invention, books were copied by hand, which was a slow process.
The internet has also greatly impacted how we access information.
The printing press allowed for mass production of books, making them more accessible.
questions.explanation: Find the sentence that is off topic. The paragraph is about the printing press, so hand-copied books and mass production belong, while 'The internet has also greatly impacted how we access information' jumps to modern technology.

questions.stem: Read the paragraph and select the sentence that doesn't belong.
options: Regular exercise is beneficial for maintaining good health.
It can improve cardiovascular fitness and strengthen muscles.
Eating fruits and vegetables provides essential nutrients.
Exercise can also help reduce stress and improve mental health.
questions.explanation: The odd sentence is the one about a different subject. Fitness, strength and stress relief all describe exercise, while eating fruits and vegetables is about diet instead.

questions.stem: Identify the sentence that does not belong in the paragraph.
options: The process of photosynthesis allows plants to convert sunlight into energy.
Chlorophyll in plant cells captures light energy.
Photosynthesis produces oxygen as a byproduct.
Some animals hibernate during the winter months.
questions.explanation: Every sentence in a paragraph should stay on one subject. Sunlight, chlorophyll and oxygen all explain photosynthesis, so the sentence about animals hibernating in winter is the one that does not belong.

questions.stem: Choose the sentence that doesn't fit in the paragraph.
options: Learning a new language can open up opportunities for travel and cultural exchange.
It can enhance cognitive abilities and improve memory.
Many people enjoy painting and drawing as hobbies.
Knowing another language can also boost career prospects.
questions.explanation: Look for the sentence that wanders off the subject. Travel, sharper thinking and better job chances are all reasons to learn a language, while painting and drawing are unrelated hobbies.

questions.stem: Read the paragraph and select the best concluding sentence.
options: Renewable energy sources are becoming increasingly important.
Solar and wind power are clean alternatives to fossil fuels.
These sources help reduce greenhouse gas emissions.
Therefore, investing in renewable energy is crucial for a sustainable future.
questions.explanation: A concluding sentence sums up what was already said and adds nothing new. 'Therefore, investing in renewable energy is crucial for a sustainable future' pulls the details together, while the sentence about growing importance is the topic sentence.

questions.stem: Choose the sentence that best concludes the paragraph.
options: Time management is a critical skill for success.
Prioritizing tasks helps ensure important deadlines are met.
Using planners or digital calendars can aid in organizing schedules.
By effectively managing time, individuals can achieve their goals more efficiently.
questions.explanation: A conclusion restates the point after the details, without adding new information. The sentence about achieving goals more efficiently wraps everything up, while 'Using planners or digital calendars can aid in organizing schedules' is only one supporting detail.

questions.stem: Select the best concluding sentence for the paragraph.
options: Reading regularly has numerous benefits.
It expands vocabulary and improves comprehension skills.
Reading can also reduce stress and provide a form of entertainment.
Therefore, incorporating reading into daily routines can greatly enhance personal development.
questions.explanation: The concluding sentence comes last and sums up the paragraph. The sentence urging readers to make reading part of daily routines does that, while 'Reading regularly has numerous benefits' is the topic sentence that starts the paragraph.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a capitalization mistake? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: The novel Pride and Prejudice is a classic.
We are going to florida for vacation.
My family visited the Grand Canyon last summer.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: "florida" is the name of a state, so it needs a capital F. Proper nouns such as states, cities and countries are always capitalized.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a capitalization mistake? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: The statue of Liberty is located in New York City.
Our teacher assigned a project on the American Revolution.
My favorite book is The Catcher in the Rye.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: "statue of Liberty" should be "Statue of Liberty." Every important word in the name of one specific monument gets a capital letter.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a capitalization mistake? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: I enjoy reading books by J.K. Rowling.
We studied the history of the medieval Period in Europe.
He lives near the University of Chicago.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: "medieval Period" should be "medieval period." A general stretch of time is not capitalized; only named periods, like the Renaissance, get capitals.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a capitalization mistake? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: My favorite sports team is the Los Angeles Lakers.
The capitol building is located in Washington, D.C.
She read The Hunger Games over the summer.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: "capitol building" should be "Capitol Building." It is the name of one specific building in Washington, D.C., so both words take capitals.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a capitalization mistake? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: We're going to the beach this Summer.
Our family is planning a trip to the Rocky Mountains.
I'm studying World History this semester.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: Seasons are not capitalized, so "this Summer" should be "this summer." "World History" is fine because it names one specific course.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a capitalization mistake? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: My aunt works in the finance department at her company.
We saw a movie called a Beautiful Mind last weekend.
They're going to visit the Eiffel Tower in France.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: "a Beautiful Mind" should be "A Beautiful Mind." The first word of a title is always capitalized, even when it is a small word like "a."

questions.stem: Which sentence has a capitalization mistake? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: We learned about the civil Rights Movement in school.
The Pacific Ocean is the largest ocean on Earth.
She works in New York City for a large company.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: "civil Rights Movement" should be "Civil Rights Movement." Named historical events and movements take a capital on every important word.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a capitalization mistake? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: He attends mass every Sunday morning.
I'm traveling to the White House next year.
The book To Kill a Mockingbird is on my reading list.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: "mass" should be "Mass" when it names the Catholic worship service. Names of specific religious services are treated as proper nouns.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a capitalization mistake? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: My brother is attending Harvard university next fall.
We studied the Constitution in our government class.
She visited Mount Rushmore with her family last year.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: "Harvard university" should be "Harvard University." When you name one specific school, the word "University" is part of that name and gets a capital.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a capitalization mistake? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: I will visit the Lincoln Memorial when I go to Washington, D.C.
The Lord of the Rings series is my favorite.
My favorite subject is Math.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: School subjects are not capitalized, so "Math" should be "math." Only languages such as Spanish and the names of specific courses keep their capital letters.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a capitalization mistake? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: My sister is studying engineering at Stanford University.
They're learning about the renaissance in history class.
I'm going to the Art Institute of Chicago this weekend.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: "renaissance" should be "Renaissance" because it names one specific period in history. Notice that "history class" correctly stays lowercase.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a capitalization mistake? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: The Mississippi River flows through several states.
Our school is visiting the smithsonian museums in Washington.
She was inspired by the play Romeo and Juliet.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: "smithsonian" should be "Smithsonian." It is the name of one specific group of museums, and names are proper nouns that need a capital letter.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a capitalization mistake? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: The Getty Museum is a popular tourist attraction in Los Angeles.
My friend loves to read about the titanic.
We visited the Empire State Building last summer.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: "the titanic" should be "the Titanic." Ships have names, and the name of a specific ship is a proper noun that needs a capital.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a capitalization mistake? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: We are planning a trip to South Africa in December.
The book Of Mice and men was a class favorite.
He's a big fan of the Dallas Cowboys.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: "Of Mice and men" should be "Of Mice and Men." In a title you capitalize the main words, and "men" is a noun, not a small joining word.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a capitalization mistake? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: The Brooklyn Bridge connects Manhattan and Brooklyn.
She's studying the Industrial revolution in her class.
My family attends Mass every Sunday.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: "Industrial revolution" should be "Industrial Revolution." A named historical event takes a capital on every important word in its name.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a capitalization mistake? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: They went to Yellowstone National Park last year.
The great wall of China is an incredible structure.
My brother is studying at the University of Texas.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: "great wall of China" should be "Great Wall of China." It names one specific landmark, so each important word in the name is capitalized.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a capitalization mistake? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: She is reading The Chronicles of Narnia for the first time.
My parents are going to Italy in the Spring.
He went to the Museum of Modern Art in New York City.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: Seasons stay lowercase, so "in the Spring" should be "in the spring." Months like December are capitalized, but spring, summer, fall and winter are not.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a capitalization mistake? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: My cousin is learning about the Roman Empire.
The book the Great Gatsby is on our reading list.
We visited the Vatican during our trip to Rome.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: "the Great Gatsby" should be "The Great Gatsby." The first word of a title is capitalized, even when that word happens to be "the."

questions.stem: Which sentence has a capitalization mistake? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: I love watching movies directed by Steven spielberg.
We learned about World War II in history class.
My sister attended Yale University last fall.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: "Steven spielberg" should be "Steven Spielberg." A person's last name is a proper noun, so it always begins with a capital letter.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a spelling mistake? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: The weatherman predictted a sunny day.
She was wearing a beautiful dress.
I took a different route to work today.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: "Predictted" should be "predicted." The word "predict" already ends in two consonants, so you just add -ed without doubling anything.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a spelling mistake? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: He received a letter in the mail.
The student answered the question correctly.
We visited several fammous landmarks during our trip.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: "Fammous" should be "famous." It comes from "fame," which has only one m, so keep one m and trade the e for -ous.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a spelling mistake? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: She was excited to finaly graduate.
The manager approved the project.
We will definitely go to the concert.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: "Finaly" should be "finally." Final plus -ly keeps both l's, one from "final" and one from the ending "-ly."

questions.stem: Which sentence has a spelling mistake? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: I accidentaly broke the glass.
They were planning a surprise party.
The teacher appreciated the students' hard work.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: "Accidentaly" should be "accidentally." Start from the adjective "accidental" and add -ly, which gives you two l's at the end.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a spelling mistake? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: The hotel had a magnificant view of the beach.
She was a strong competitor in the race.
We had to cancel the appointment.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: "Magnificant" should be "magnificent." This word ends in -ent, the same way "excellent" and "different" do.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a spelling mistake? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: The temperature droped overnight.
He always gave great advice to his friends.
I don’t know how to maneuver the new equipment.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: "Droped" should be "dropped." When a short word ends in one vowel plus one consonant, double that consonant before adding -ed.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a spelling mistake? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: She was given an award for her acheivements.
The children were playing outside in the field.
He had to rewrite his entire essay.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: "Acheivements" should be "achievements." Use the old rhyme, i before e except after c, to remember that the base word is "achieve."

questions.stem: Which sentence has a spelling mistake? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: We visited a beautiful villiage by the sea.
The children were building sandcastles on the beach.
The mountain was covered in snow.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: "Villiage" should be "village." There is no i after the two l's; think of the word as "vill" plus "age."

questions.stem: Which sentence has a spelling mistake? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: She was gratefull for the support of her family.
They traveled to a distant city for the festival.
The hotel had a grand entrance.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: "Gratefull" should be "grateful." The ending -ful has only one l, just like it does in "helpful" and "careful."

questions.stem: Which sentence has a spelling mistake? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: The counsil met to discuss the new regulations.
She loves to read historical novels.
The cat chased the mouse across the room.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: "Counsil" should be "council." A council is a group that meets, and it ends in -cil. Do not mix it up with "counsel," which means advice.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a spelling mistake? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: The chef prepared a delisious meal.
We walked along the beach as the sun set.
He received a gift from his parents.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: "Delisious" should be "delicious." The "sh" sound in the middle is spelled with a c here, the same as in "precious" and "suspicious."

questions.stem: Which sentence has a spelling mistake? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: The policemen worked together to solve the case.
She had a large collection of jewelry.
The man was convicted of burgulary.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: "Burgulary" should be "burglary." There is no u after the g; the word is simply "burglar" with a y on the end.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a spelling mistake? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: The sun shone brightly over the horizen.
They were concerned about the environment.
He always carried a notebook to write down ideas.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: "Horizen" should be "horizon." The last syllable uses an o, which you can hear clearly in the longer word "horizontal."

questions.stem: Which sentence has a spelling mistake? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: He had to apoligize for his mistake.
The patient was recovering after surgery.
They lost their way in the labyrinth of streets.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: "Apoligize" should be "apologize." It comes from "apology," so the middle letter is an o, not an i.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a spelling mistake? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: The goverment passed new laws to protect wildlife.
She organized her closet over the weekend.
The cat knocked over the vase.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: "Goverment" should be "government." Say it slowly as "govern" plus "-ment" and you will hear the n that is so easy to drop.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a spelling mistake? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: The doctor gave a perscription for the medication.
The project required a great deal of coordination.
He was an excellent student throughout high school.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: "Perscription" should be "prescription." It begins with "pre-," like "prescribe," because the doctor writes the order before you get the medicine.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a spelling mistake? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: She read the instructions before starting the experimant.
The company was known for its innovations.
We explored the museum for hours.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: "Experimant" should be "experiment." The ending is -ment, the same ending you see in "movement" and "argument."

questions.stem: Which sentence has a spelling mistake? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: They used binoculars to see the stars clearer.
The store offers a variety of organic products.
I will meet you at the restaurant at six o'clock.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: Every word here is spelled correctly, including the tricky ones: "binoculars," "variety" and "restaurant." Nothing in these sentences needs a spelling fix.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a spelling mistake? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: The comittee voted on the proposal.
He was known for his kindness and generosity.
She presented a well-researched report.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: "Comittee" should be "committee." This word has a double m, a double t and a double e, so think of it as the word with three pairs.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a spelling mistake? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: The artist sketched a beautifull portrait.
They decided to stay at the cabin for the weekend.
The children played in the backyard.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: "Beautifull" should be "beautiful." The ending -ful is spelled with one l when it is added to a word, just like in "wonderful" and "colorful."

questions.stem: Which sentence has a mistake in grammar or usage? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: She don't like to eat vegetables.
They are planning a trip next month.
We will meet at the park after school.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: The pronoun "She" is singular, so it takes "doesn't," not "don't." The sentence should read "She doesn't like to eat vegetables." The other verbs match their plural subjects.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a mistake in grammar or usage? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: She has written a novel.
He has ran the marathon three times.
They have traveled to many countries.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: After "has," the verb run uses its past participle "run," not "ran," so it should be "He has run the marathon." The participles "written" and "traveled" are correct.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a mistake in grammar or usage? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: She shared the cookies with her friends.
He walked between the two buildings.
Between you and I, I think the test was difficult.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: After a preposition like "between," use an object pronoun, so "Between you and I" should be "Between you and me." The other two sentences are correct as written.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a mistake in grammar or usage? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: Neither the coach nor the players were happy with the result.
Neither the coach nor the players was happy with the result.
Neither the cat nor the dog likes loud noises.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: With "neither ... nor," the verb matches the subject closer to it. "Players" is plural, so "Neither the coach nor the players was happy" needs "were happy" instead.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a mistake in grammar or usage? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: He should have studied harder for the exam.
She would have called if she had the time.
He should of studied harder for the exam.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: The phrase "should of" is never correct; it just copies the sound of "should've." The sentence needs "He should have studied harder." The other two use "have" and "had" correctly.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a mistake in grammar or usage? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: I feel bad about your situation.
She feels happy today.
He feels sick after eating too much candy.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: All three sentences are fine, so choose "No mistakes." After a linking verb like feel, you use an adjective, so "feel bad," "feels happy" and "feels sick" are all right.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a mistake in grammar or usage? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: There is less students in the class this year.
There are fewer apples in the basket.
He has less time than before.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: Students can be counted, so "less students" should be "fewer students," and the plural subject also needs "There are." The phrases "fewer apples" and "less time" are correct.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a mistake in grammar or usage? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: He didn't do anything wrong.
She doesn't have any money left.
They don't know anyone at the party.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: All three sentences are fine, so choose "No mistakes." Each one uses a single negative paired with "anything," "any" or "anyone," so none of them doubles its negatives.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a mistake in grammar or usage? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: He couldn't care less about the outcome.
He could care less about the outcome.
They couldn't agree on a decision.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: The idiom is "couldn't care less," meaning your caring cannot go any lower. "He could care less about the outcome" accidentally says the opposite of what is meant.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a mistake in grammar or usage? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: I did well on the test.
She did well in the competition.
I did good on the test.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: The word "good" is an adjective, but the verb "did" needs an adverb, so "I did good on the test" should be "I did well." The other two sentences already use "well."

questions.stem: Which sentence has a mistake in grammar or usage? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: Each of the books is on the shelf.
Every one of the books is on the shelf.
All of the books are on the shelf.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: All three sentences are fine, so choose "No mistakes." "Each" and "every one" are singular and take "is," while "all of the books" is plural and takes "are."

questions.stem: Which sentence has a mistake in grammar or usage? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: Whose going to the game tonight?
Who's bringing the snacks?
Whose jacket is this?
No mistakes
questions.explanation: The word "whose" shows possession and "who's" means "who is," so "Whose going to the game" should be "Who's going." "Who's bringing" and "Whose jacket" are both right.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a mistake in grammar or usage? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: He gave the book to me.
He gave the book to myself.
They asked us to join them.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: Use "myself" only when you are also the subject, as in "I gave myself a break." Here it should be "He gave the book to me." The other two pronouns are used correctly.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a mistake in grammar or usage? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: The team played well in the tournament.
She sings beautifully on stage.
The team played good in the tournament.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: The word "played" is an action verb, so it needs the adverb "well," not the adjective "good." The other two sentences use "well" and "beautifully" correctly.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a mistake in grammar or usage? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: If I were taller, I could reach the shelf.
If she were here, she would help us.
If they were ready, we could start.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: All three sentences are fine, so choose "No mistakes." For an imagined or untrue situation, English uses "were" with every subject, so "If I were" and "If she were" are right.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a mistake in grammar or usage? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: Between my brother and me, we have five trophies.
Between my brother and myself, we have five trophies.
She and I went to the store.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: After "between," use an object pronoun. "Between my brother and myself" should be "between my brother and me," because "myself" works only when you are the subject too.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a mistake in grammar or usage? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: He didn't know where he was at.
She asked where the library was.
They wondered where their friends had gone.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: The word "at" is not needed after "where," so "where he was at" should be "where he was." The other two sentences end their where-clauses correctly.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a mistake in grammar or usage? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: I have fewer coins than you do.
She has fewer pencils than before.
I have less coins than you do.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: Coins can be counted one by one, so they take "fewer," not "less." "I have less coins than you do" should be "I have fewer coins." The other two sentences use "fewer."

questions.stem: Which sentence has a mistake in grammar or usage? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: He gave the book to she and I.
He gave the book to her and me.
They invited us to their party.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: Pronouns after "to" must be object pronouns, so "to she and I" should be "to her and me." The other sentences already use "her and me" and "us" correctly.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a mistake in grammar or usage? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: I need to lay down for a while.
Please lay the book on the table.
I think I'll lie down for a bit.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: You lie down yourself, but you lay something else down. "I need to lay down" should be "I need to lie down." "Lay the book" and "I'll lie down" are both correct.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a mistake in grammar or usage? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: There are a number of reasons why we should go.
The number of participants is increasing.
A large amount of people attended the event.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: Use "number" for things you can count and "amount" for things you cannot, so "A large amount of people" should be "a large number of people." The other two sentences are fine.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a mistake in grammar or usage? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: She did good on the test.
He performed well in the game.
They sang beautifully during the concert.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: The word "did" is an action verb, so it needs the adverb "well," not the adjective "good." "She did good on the test" should be "She did well on the test."

questions.stem: Which sentence has a mistake in grammar or usage? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: If I was you, I would apologize.
If I were you, I would apologize.
If she were here, she would help.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: For a wish or an untrue situation, use "were," not "was," so "If I was you" should be "If I were you." The very next sentence shows the correct form.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a mistake in grammar or usage? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: He didn't bring nothing to the party.
She couldn't find her keys anywhere.
They had no idea what to expect.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: One negative word is enough. "He didn't bring nothing" uses two, so it should be "He didn't bring anything." The other two sentences each use a single negative.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a mistake in grammar or usage? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: He and I are going to the store.
Me and him are going to the store.
She and I will meet you there.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: A subject needs subject pronouns, so "Me and him are going" should be "He and I are going." Check each alone: you would say "I am going," not "Me am going."

questions.stem: Which sentence has a mistake in grammar or usage? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: The book, that is on the table, is mine.
The book that is on the table is mine.
The car, which is red, is fast.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: A "that" clause tells you which book, so it is essential and takes no commas: "The book that is on the table is mine." A "which" clause, like the one about the red car, does take commas.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a mistake in grammar or usage? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: Irregardless of the weather, we will proceed.
Regardless of the weather, we will proceed.
We will proceed, weather permitting.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: The word "irregardless" is not standard, because the ir- prefix and the -less ending both make it negative. Use "regardless," exactly as the second sentence does.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a mistake in grammar or usage? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: She is real talented.
He is really excited about the trip.
They are very happy to be here.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: The word "real" is an adjective, but "talented" needs an adverb, so "She is real talented" should be "She is really talented." "Really excited" and "very happy" are correct.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a mistake in grammar or usage? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: I can't hardly wait for summer vacation.
I can hardly wait for summer vacation.
She could barely see in the dark room.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: The word "hardly" already means almost not, so "can't hardly wait" is a double negative. It should be "I can hardly wait," just as the next sentence shows.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a mistake in grammar or usage? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: He is the eldest of the two brothers.
She is the taller of the two sisters.
They are the best players on the team.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: Comparing exactly two people calls for the comparative, so "the eldest of the two brothers" should be "the elder of the two brothers." "The taller of the two sisters" is correct.

questions.stem: Which sentence has a mistake in grammar or usage? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: Neither of the answers are correct.
Neither of the answers is correct.
Either option is acceptable.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: The word "neither" is singular, so it takes "is," not "are." "Neither of the answers are correct" should be "Neither of the answers is correct."

questions.stem: Which sentence has a mistake in grammar or usage? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: He has less coins than I do.
She has fewer coins than I do.
They have fewer problems now.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: Coins can be counted one by one, so they take "fewer," not "less." "He has less coins than I do" should be "He has fewer coins than I do."

questions.stem: Which sentence has a mistake in grammar or usage? If all three are correct, choose “No mistakes.”
options: She set the book on the table.
He sat down to rest.
She sat the vase on the shelf.
No mistakes
questions.explanation: The verb "set" means to place something, while "sat" means to take a seat. "She sat the vase on the shelf" should be "She set the vase on the shelf."

questions.stem: Which sentence is written correctly?
options: Me and him went to the store yesterday.
He and I went to the store yesterday.
Him and I went to the store yesterday.
He and me went to the store yesterday.
questions.explanation: "He and I went to the store yesterday" is right, because a subject needs subject pronouns. Test each one alone: "He went" and "I went" work, but "Me went" and "Him went" do not.

questions.stem: Which sentence is written correctly?
options: She don't like apples.
She doesn't likes apples.
She doesn't like apples.
She don't likes apples.
questions.explanation: "She doesn't like apples" is correct. The singular subject "she" takes "doesn't," and after "doesn't" the main verb stays in its plain form, "like."

questions.stem: Which sentence is written correctly?
options: The book is laying on the table.
The book is lying on the table.
The book is lay on the table.
The book is lie on the table.
questions.explanation: "The book is lying on the table" is right. Lie means to rest in place, and its -ing form is "lying"; "laying" would need an object, as in laying a book down.

questions.stem: Which sentence is written correctly?
options: The team are celebrating its victory.
The team is celebrating their victory.
The team is celebrating its victory.
The team are celebrating their victory.
questions.explanation: "The team is celebrating its victory" is right. In American English a team counts as one unit, so it takes the singular verb "is" and the singular pronoun "its."

questions.stem: Which sentence is written correctly?
options: If I was rich, I would travel the world.
If I were rich, I would travel the world.
If I am rich, I would travel the world.
If I be rich, I would travel the world.
questions.explanation: "If I were rich, I would travel the world" is correct. For something imaginary or untrue, English uses "were" with every subject, including "I."

questions.stem: Which sentence is written correctly?
options: Between you and I, I think he's wrong.
Between you and me, I think he's wrong.
Between you and myself, I think he's wrong.
Between you and mine, I think he's wrong.
questions.explanation: "Between you and me, I think he's wrong" is correct. "Between" is a preposition, and prepositions take object pronouns, so "I," "myself" and "mine" do not fit.

questions.stem: Which sentence is written correctly?
options: Whom is calling me at this hour?
Who is calling me at this hour?
Whose is calling me at this hour?
Whom are calling me at this hour?
questions.explanation: "Who is calling me at this hour?" is right. "Who" is the subject doing the calling; "whom" is only for objects and "whose" shows who owns something.

questions.stem: Which sentence is written correctly?
options: She is the taller of the three sisters.
She is the tallest of the three sisters.
She is the most tall of the three sisters.
She is taller than any sister.
questions.explanation: "She is the tallest of the three sisters" is correct. With three or more, use the superlative ending -est; "taller" is only for comparing two.

questions.stem: Which sentence is written correctly?
options: He is responsible of completing the report.
He is responsible for completing the report.
He is responsible to completing the report.
He is responsible about completing the report.
questions.explanation: "He is responsible for completing the report" is correct. In this meaning, the adjective "responsible" always pairs with the preposition "for."

questions.stem: Which sentence is written correctly?
options: Neither of the options are good.
Neither of the options is good.
Neither of the options were good.
Neither of the options have been good.
questions.explanation: "Neither of the options is good" is correct. "Neither" is singular, so it takes a singular verb even when a plural phrase like "of the options" comes after it.

questions.stem: Which sentence is written correctly?
options: She sings beautiful.
She sings beautifully.
She sings beautifuly.
She sings beauty.
questions.explanation: "She sings beautifully" is correct. Sings is an action verb, so it needs the adverb form, which keeps the l in beautiful and adds -ly.

questions.stem: Which sentence is written correctly?
options: The cat chased it's tail.
The cat chased its tail.
The cat chased its' tail.
The cat chased it tail.
questions.explanation: "The cat chased its tail" is correct. The possessive "its" takes no apostrophe, "it's" is short for "it is" or "it has," and "its'" is never a word.

questions.stem: Which sentence is written correctly?
options: She arrived to the party at 8 PM.
She arrived at the party at 8 PM.
She arrived in the party at 8 PM.
She arrived on the party at 8 PM.
questions.explanation: "She arrived at the party at 8 PM" is correct. In English you arrive at a place or an event; you do not arrive to it or on it.

questions.stem: Which sentence is written correctly?
options: I'm looking forward to see you.
I'm looking forward to seeing you.
I'm looking forward seeing you.
I'm looking forward for seeing you.
questions.explanation: "I'm looking forward to seeing you" is correct. Here "to" is a preposition, not part of the verb, and a verb after a preposition takes the -ing form.

questions.stem: Which sentence is written correctly?
options: The amount of people at the concert was overwhelming.
The number of people at the concert was overwhelming.
The number of people at the concert were overwhelming.
The amount of people at the concert were overwhelming.
questions.explanation: "The number of people at the concert was overwhelming" is correct. People can be counted, so use "number," not "amount," and "the number" is singular, so it takes "was."

questions.stem: Which sentence is written correctly?
options: He did good on the test.
He did well on the test.
He did goodly on the test.
He did welly on the test.
questions.explanation: "He did well on the test" is correct. "Did" is an action verb and needs the adverb "well"; "good" is an adjective, and "goodly" and "welly" are not real options here.

questions.stem: Which sentence is written correctly?
options: I have less friends than she does.
I have fewer friends than she does.
I have few friends than she does.
I have lesser friends than she does.
questions.explanation: "I have fewer friends than she does" is correct. Friends can be counted one by one, so they take "fewer"; "less" is for amounts you cannot count, like water.

questions.stem: Which sentence is written correctly?
options: The news are on at 6 PM.
The news is on at 6 PM.
The news have been on at 6 PM.
The news were on at 6 PM.
questions.explanation: "The news is on at 6 PM" is correct. The word news ends in s but names one thing, so it is singular and takes a singular verb.

questions.stem: Which sentence is written correctly?
options: She is the most fastest runner on the team.
She is the fastest runner on the team.
She is the most fast runner on the team.
She is the faster runner on the team.
questions.explanation: "She is the fastest runner on the team" is correct. Short adjectives add -est to make the superlative, and you never pile "most" on top of that ending.

questions.stem: Which sentence is written correctly?
options: He is capable to finish the job.
He is capable of finishing the job.
He is capable for finishing the job.
He is capable in finishing the job.
questions.explanation: "He is capable of finishing the job" is correct. "Capable" always pairs with "of," and a verb that follows "of" takes the -ing form.

questions.stem: Which sentence is written correctly?
options: She did it by herself.
She did it by her own.
She did it by her.
She did it by she.
questions.explanation: "She did it by herself" is correct. The phrase "by herself" means alone, and it needs the reflexive pronoun "herself," not "her," "she" or "her own."

questions.stem: Which sentence is written correctly?
options: The committee has reached their decision.
The committee have reached its decision.
The committee has reached its decision.
The committee have reached their decision.
questions.explanation: "The committee has reached its decision" is correct. In American English a committee is one group, so it takes the singular verb "has" and the singular pronoun "its."

questions.stem: Which sentence is written correctly?
options: I will call you when I will arrive.
I will call you when I arrive.
I will call you when I will be arriving.
I will call you when I will have arrived.
questions.explanation: "I will call you when I arrive" is correct. After a time word like when, English uses the present tense for a future action instead of a second "will."

questions.stem: Which sentence is written correctly?
options: Each of the players have a locker.
Each of the players has a locker.
Each of the players have lockers.
Each of the players has lockers.
questions.explanation: "Each of the players has a locker" is correct. "Each" is singular, so it takes "has," and each single player owns one locker.

questions.stem: Which sentence is written correctly?
options: I'm not sure weather he is coming or not.
I'm not sure whether he is coming or not.
I'm not sure rather he is coming nor not.
I'm not sure if he is coming nor not.
questions.explanation: "I'm not sure whether he is coming or not" is correct. "Whether" sets up two choices; "weather" means rain and sunshine, and "rather" does not fit here.
